turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come through. What's the problem today?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): This rash, it's come up all red and I cannot stop scratching, and I don't know if it was something I ate or the new cream or the antibiotic, and I'm really frightened it's—
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did it start?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, yesterday afternoon I think, or maybe the night before, I was round at my sister's and—
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yesterday. Whereabouts on you?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Tummy, both arms, and a bit on the neck. Red, blotchy, so itchy I barely slept a wink.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Lips, tongue or eyelids swollen?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No swelling at all.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any trouble breathing?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): We had garlic prawns, a huge plate, I don't usually eat that many, and then I felt a bit off but I thought—
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll ask about the food in a minute. Breathing — tight, wheezy, short of breath?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None of that. Breathing's been alright.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't feel hot. I checked.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vomiting or diarrhoea?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Name of the antibiotic?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): I got this new cream, Advantan, the fatty ointment, from the chemist for my hands because my eczema's been playing up, started it Sunday, and I wonder if that's what—
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Antibiotic. Name, and the day you started.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry. Amoxicillin, from the dentist, for a tooth infection. Started Monday.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): What dose?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Five hundred milligrams, three times a day. I did two days, then I stopped it last night. Didn't take the bedtime dose. Too scared.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stopped completely?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Stopped. I'm not taking any more.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Still using the Advantan?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Sunday and Monday on my hands only. Nothing since the rash. So I've stopped that as well. Was that wrong? Should I have kept going?
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stopped is fine for now. Any other new food?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Prawns Saturday night at my sister's in Preston. And mango at lunch yesterday, but I eat mango all the time, so that isn't it, is it? Can mango even do this?
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mango's unlikely if it's never bothered you. Other regular medicines?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Perindopril four milligrams every morning for my blood pressure, been on it for years. And vitamin D sometimes, when I remember.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vitamin D — how much, how often?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know the strength. Maybe twice a week? I'm not even sure I took it this week.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Forget the vitamin D. Were you given prednisolone?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): The dentist talked about a steroid tablet but I never filled the script. Never took a single one.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Drug allergies?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing. I'm not allergic to anything.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Old note. Your mum told this clinic you got a rash from penicillin as a child.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No she didn't — I mean, she says that, but it's wrong. That was my brother, not me. I've had amoxicillin before and I was fine. I am not allergic to penicillin.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): You deny it. The note says you had it. We can't sort that argument today.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): So am I allergic or not? If the dentist gave me amoxicillin and I am allergic, is that his mistake, and what happens next time I need an antibiotic, and—
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not today. Let me examine you.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): It's worse on the stomach. Are they hives? I looked it up and hives can be dangerous, can't they, and—
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Raised red patches over the abdomen and both forearms. No blisters. No peeling skin.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): What about the neck, did you see the neck?
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Neck's mildly pink. Throat is clear. Chest clear, no wheeze.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse eighty-eight. Blood pressure one twenty-eight over seventy-six. Temp thirty-six point eight. Oxygen sat ninety-eight percent on air.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Is eighty-eight bad? My heart's been thumping because I'm anxious, is that the reaction, do I need emergency, because online it said—
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse is acceptable. This is not an emergency.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Um, actually, going back to swelling, I said no, but—
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Go on.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): My eyelids were puffy when I woke up. Both of them. Still a bit puffy sitting here. I blamed not sleeping.
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Both eyelids are mildly swollen. Agreed.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that anaphylaxis? That's how people die, isn't it? Am I going to be okay, doctor, honestly?
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not anaphylaxis. You're speaking in full sentences, breathing is easy, pressure is normal. Rash plus mild eyelid swelling.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): My tongue feels tingly since last night. It comes and goes. It's not swollen, just odd. Is tingling the start of the throat closing?
[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tongue looks normal, not swollen. Tingling on its own is not the throat closing.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tummy pain?
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Joint pains?
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): No, joints are good. I was wiped out yesterday though, and I'm exhausted now. Is being this tired part of an allergic thing?
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tiredness can go with it. I can't say whether the cause is the amoxicillin, the Advantan, or the prawns. All three are possible. No firm diagnosis.

[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Then which do I avoid? If I pick the wrong one it'll happen again, and what if it's all three, and is a tiny bit of Advantan enough to do this, and can I ever have prawns at Christmas—
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stop the amoxicillin. Do not restart it. Stop the Advantan too.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): My eczema will crack if I stop. What am I supposed to put on my hands?
[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): Plain sorbolene only. No new creams.
[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): And the prawns? And mango? I have mango in the fridge, do I throw it out?
[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): Avoid prawns until this settles. Keep the mango. It's not the suspect.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): What can you give me for the itch? I can't do another night of this, it's like ants under the skin, I have work at six—
[SEG0069] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cetirizine ten milligrams, once a day, by mouth. Start tonight.
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): With perindopril? Is that safe? Will it knock me out? I drive to the warehouse at six in the morning.
[SEG0071] person_1 (DOCTOR): Safe with perindopril. It can make you sleepy. Take it at night, not in the morning.
[SEG0072] person_2 (PATIENT): What if the chemist only has the five milligram tablets? Do I take two? Is ten too much for someone my size?
[SEG0073] person_1 (DOCTOR): Two of the five milligram tablets at night. That is ten milligrams. Dose stands.
[SEG0074] person_2 (PATIENT): And if the cetirizine doesn't work, then what, do I just suffer?
[SEG0075] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the rash is no better in three days, book back in with me.
[SEG0076] person_2 (PATIENT): Shouldn't there be a blood test? Or an allergy test? I want proof of which thing did it. Can't you just order something today?
[SEG0077] person_1 (DOCTOR): No blood test today. If it keeps happening, or we need to sort the cream, patch testing can be arranged later. Not booked now.
[SEG0078] person_2 (PATIENT): Patch testing, that's the stickers on your back, right? Does it hurt? How many days does it take? Can I work with them on?
[SEG0079] person_1 (DOCTOR): Patches on the back, checked at forty-eight hours. Only if we need them. Not today.
[SEG0080] person_2 (PATIENT): And you still won't tell me if penicillin is safe. So I might be allergic and you're sending me home?
[SEG0081] person_1 (DOCTOR): Penicillin testing is a separate clinic test, and only if that old story stands up. Your mum says yes. You say no. Park it.

[SEG0082] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. I'll stop the amoxicillin and the Advantan, cetirizine tonight, no prawns, and I'll come back if I'm not better in three days. If my tongue swells or I can't breathe I go straight to emergency, yes?
[SEG0083] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. Emergency if the tongue or the lips swell further, breathing gets difficult, or you feel faint. Otherwise, three days if it's not settling. That's us done.
